title: Built-in control flow (@if/@for), not *ngIf/*ngFor
statement: Templates use the built-in `@if`/`@for`/`@switch` blocks. New code does not add `*ngIf`/`*ngFor`/`*ngSwitch`, and does not import `CommonModule` just to get them.
rationale: Built-in control flow is what the rest of the app already uses (`review-panel.html` is entirely `@if`/`@for`); it compiles to more efficient instructions than the structural-directive form and doesn't require a `CommonModule` import on an otherwise-standalone component. Mixing both forms in one codebase means a reader has to know two syntaxes for the same thing.

good.code:
@if (api.reviewError()) {
{{ api.reviewError() }}
} @for (run of scopeRuns(); track run.id) { ... }
good.caption: Built-in control flow throughout.

bad.code:
{{ error }}
...
bad.caption: Legacy structural directives requiring a CommonModule import.

changelog.summary: Initial rule. autofixable: true because Angular ships an official migration schematic (ng generate @angular/core:control-flow) for this exact transform.
